findings.issue_text: **Stored XSS: imported content is rendered raw with zero HTML sanitization, and is reachable by unauthenticated users.**
`app/models/post.rb:130-137` — when `cook_method == raw_html`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim, completely bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`).
`app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16` — `<%= raw post.cooked %>` renders that unsanitized content directly, without escaping, to any anonymous visitor of `/embed/best`.

`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36-39` — RSS feed item content (`i.content`) is unescaped via `CGI.unescapeHTML` and handed straight to `TopicEmbed.import` with **no tag/attribute allowlist at all** (unlike `import_remote`, which at least constrains Readability's output to a tag/attribute list). Any `<script>` in a polled feed item becomes a stored, rendered payload.

`app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "` interpolates `url` into an HTML attribute/text **without escaping**. `url` is attacker-influenced: `EmbedController#best` accepts `embed_url` from a public request param, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only validates the *host* component (`URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) — the path/query string is fully attacker-controlled. An unauthenticated request such as `GET /embed/best?embed_url=http:///x?y='>` will pass host validation, get queued via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` → `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, and the raw `embed_url` string is spliced unescaped into the post body that is then persisted and rendered `raw` to every visitor of that embed.
**Why it matters**: this is a persistent, unauthenticated, remotely-triggerable XSS against any site that enables comment embedding — the exact feature this PR ships.

**How to fix**: never store/render attacker- or feed-derived HTML without sanitization even under `raw_html`. Run `TopicEmbed.import`'s `contents` (both the RSS-polled body and the Readability-extracted body) through an allowlist sanitizer (the `sanitize` gem is already a dependency) before persisting, and HTML-escape `url`/`title` wherever they're interpolated into markup (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape(url)` in the "imported from" line). Also constrain `href`/`src` schemes to `http(s)` to prevent `javascript:` URIs from surviving into `<a href>`.
**Regression: `disqus.thor` import loses the ability to target a category.**

`lib/tasks/disqus.thor` — the `-c/--category` option and its `category_id` lookup were removed, and the replacement call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` has no way to pass a category (`TopicEmbed.import`'s `PostCreator.new` call never threads a `category` option). Existing users of this migration script silently lose a feature.

**How to fix**: either add an optional `category` param to `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote` and thread it through from the thor task, or explicitly note the removal as an intentional breaking change.
**`disqus.thor` import now depends on live network fetches per thread, with no error handling.**

Previously, import only needed the stored permalink text; now `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` for every thread. If any of the (potentially thousands of) old links is unreachable, renamed, or 404s, the exception is unhandled and aborts the entire migration run partway through, with no resumption story.
**How to fix**: wrap the fetch in a `begin/rescue`, log/skip failures, and let the rest of the import continue.
**`TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicRetriever#fetch_http` perform server-side fetches of attacker-influenced URLs (open-uri, default redirect-following).**

`app/models/topic_embed.rb:29` (`open(url).read`) — the host must match `embeddable_host`, but path/query is attacker-controlled, and `open-uri` follows redirects by default; a malicious or compromised target page could redirect the server to internal/other resources (SSRF surface). Given this era's `open-uri`, this is worth hardening rather than assuming it's safe.
**How to fix**: pin `open-uri` behavior (disable redirects or validate the redirect target's host as well), and/or use a proper HTTP client with an explicit allowlist and timeout.
**Test coverage gaps for the actual new business logic.**
`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests the three guard conditions in `execute`; the body of `poll_feed` (RSS parsing, `TopicEmbed.import` per item, URL fallback to `i.id`) is never exercised.
`TopicEmbed.import_remote` (Readability integration) has no spec at all.
`TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` is only indirectly exercised via the `import` spec for anchor/img rewriting on create, not on update, and not for edge cases (missing scheme, non-default ports).

**Why it matters**: these are precisely the code paths carrying untrusted external content (see Critical #1) — they need direct tests, including a security-oriented test asserting dangerous tags/attributes are stripped.
`app/models/topic_embed.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` uses Rails' dependency-tracking require on a third-party gem; should just be `require 'nokogiri'`.
`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused dead code (nothing in the file references `Email::Sender`).

`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15` — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check rather than an exact-origin comparison; prefer `e.origin !== discourseUrl` (or compare parsed origins) for a precise, non-surprising check even though `discourseUrl` isn't attacker-controlled here.
`config/locales/server.en.yml` — `embed.permalink` key is added but never referenced anywhere in the views/models.

`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb` — `ensure_embeddable` only supports a single `embeddable_host`; no path to allow multiple embedding domains without redeploying config. Consider a comma-separated list if that's a plausible near-term need.

`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best` — if `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns a stale `topic_id` for a topic that's since been deleted/made private, `TopicView.new` will raise unrescued (500 instead of a graceful "not found"/loading state).

Several new files (`embed.css.scss`, `loading.html.erb`, `layouts/embed.html.erb`, `topic_retriever.rb`) are missing trailing newlines — trivial, but flagged since it's inconsistent with the rest of the diff.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Stored XSS: imported content is rendered raw with zero HTML sanitization, and is reachable by unauthenticated users.**

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cook_method` that can bypass the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using `contents` pulled from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and `i.content`) or from remote HTML via `Readability::Document` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` reads `open(url).read`), and does not sanitize this HTML before saving. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any embedded scripts/unsafe attributes would execute (stored XSS). The embed endpoint uses `current_user` which can be nil (spec expects `TopicView.new(123, nil, ...)`), and no authentication requirement is shown for `EmbedController#best`, making the XSS reachable to unauthenticated visitors as long as the referer host check passes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/post.rb:130-137` — when `cook_method == raw_html`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim, completely bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the existing cooking pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) that normally renders/sanitizes content. The new embedding/import path (`TopicEmbed.import` / `import_remote`) sets `cook_method: :raw_html` for imported external HTML and `embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Since `post.cooked` will equal unsanitized `post.raw` in this mode, this introduces a clear XSS/correctness risk from remote feed/article HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16` — `<%= raw post.cooked %>` renders that unsanitized content directly, without escaping, to any anonymous visitor of `/embed/best`.

adjudication.rationale: The view renders `raw post.cooked`, which bypasses Rails escaping. In this diff, posts imported via RSS/remote embedding can be created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (see `TopicEmbed.import`), and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds `TopicEmbed.import` with `i.content` from an external feed with no HTML sanitization. Therefore `post.cooked` for these imported posts can contain attacker-controlled HTML/JS and is rendered directly in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, creating a verifiable XSS risk for users who can load the embed page (subject to the referer/embeddable_host check).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36-39` — RSS feed item content (`i.content`) is unescaped via `CGI.unescapeHTML` and handed straight to `TopicEmbed.import` with **no tag/attribute allowlist at all** (unlike `import_remote`, which at least constrains Readability's output to a tag/attribute list). Any `<script>` in a polled feed item becomes a stored, rendered payload.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job takes `i.content`, runs `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it directly to `TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`. As a result, any HTML (including `<script>` or event-handler attributes) present in the feed content—or encoded as entities and then unescaped—can become stored and rendered, unlike `import_remote` which restricts tags/attributes via Readability.

An unauthenticated request such as `GET /embed/best?embed_url=http:///x?y='>` will pass host validation, get queued via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` → `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, and the raw `embed_url` string is spliced unescaped into the post body that is then persisted and rendered `raw` to every visitor of that embed.
**Why it matters**: this is a persistent, unauthenticated, remotely-triggerable XSS against any site that enables comment embedding — the exact feature this PR ships.

**How to fix**: never store/render attacker- or feed-derived HTML without sanitization even under `raw_html`. Run `TopicEmbed.import`'s `contents` (both the RSS-polled body and the Readability-extracted body) through an allowlist sanitizer (the `sanitize` gem is already a dependency) before persisting, and HTML-escape `url`/`title` wherever they're interpolated into markup (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape(url)` in the "imported from" line). Also constrain `href`/`src` schemes to `http(s)` to prevent `javascript:` URIs from surviving into `<a href>`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method that explicitly bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`). `TopicEmbed.import` uses this mode for RSS/remote imports (`PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`), and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked`. Both RSS-polled content (`PollFeed`: `i.content.scrub` / `CGI.unescapeHTML`) and Readability-extracted content (`TopicEmbed.import_remote`: `doc.content`) are attacker/feed-derived HTML and are persisted/rendered without sanitization. Additionally, `contents` is appended with an HTML snippet containing `url` interpolated directly into an `<a href='...'>` attribute without escaping, and the only URL check is `/^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quote-breaking or other HTML injection inside the attribute. `absolutize_urls` does not constrain `href`/`src` schemes (it only rewrites leading `/`), so `javascript:` or `data:` URIs already present in imported HTML would survive. This is a concrete XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Regression: `disqus.thor` import loses the ability to target a category.**

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `:category` Thor option from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the logic that looked up `category_id` from `options[:category]`. It also replaces the `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` call with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not pass or accept a category. Therefore the Disqus import task can no longer target a category, which is a functional regression introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` — the `-c/--category` option and its `category_id` lookup were removed, and the replacement call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` has no way to pass a category (`TopicEmbed.import`'s `PostCreator.new` call never threads a `category` option). Existing users of this migration script silently lose a feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the `category_id` lookup plus passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)`. The replacement `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` ultimately calls `TopicEmbed.import`, whose `PostCreator.new(...)` invocation does not include any `category` argument (only `title`, `raw`, `skip_validations`, `cook_method`). Therefore the Thor task no longer has any mechanism to import into a user-specified category, which is a concrete behavior/feature regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **How to fix**: either add an optional `category` param to `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote` and thread it through from the thor task, or explicitly note the removal as an intentional breaking change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `:category` CLI option from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator` (`category: category_id`). The import path is replaced with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`, which has no way to accept or apply a category. This is a concrete regression/breaking change in the Thor task’s behavior/API: users can no longer import Disqus threads into a specified category, and the diff contains no comment or alternative mechanism indicating this is intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`disqus.thor` import now depends on live network fetches per thread, with no error handling.**

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import flow was changed from creating a local post with the thread link to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` for each thread. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` to fetch the remote page content and does not rescue network/HTTP errors (e.g., timeouts, 404s, DNS failures). This makes the import depend on live network fetches per thread and can cause the task to fail or abort on transient network issues without error handling in the task or model method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Previously, import only needed the stored permalink text; now `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` for every thread. If any of the (potentially thousands of) old links is unreachable, renamed, or 404s, the exception is unhandled and aborts the entire migration run partway through, with no resumption story.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes the Disqus import task to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` for each thread (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor`). `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (via `open-uri`) without any `rescue` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). If any link is unreachable/404/timeout/DNS failure, `open` can raise (e.g., `OpenURI::HTTPError`, `SocketError`), which will bubble up and abort the entire Thor import run mid-loop. There is no error handling or retry/resume logic shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **How to fix**: wrap the fetch in a `begin/rescue`, log/skip failures, and let the rest of the import continue.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetching/parsing without any error handling: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Both `open-uri` and parsing can raise (timeouts, DNS failures, non-200 responses, invalid feed/HTML), which would crash the job/task. In `PollFeed`, `sidekiq_options retry: false` makes this particularly impactful because a transient error will abort the run with no automatic retry, rather than being logged/skipped and continuing future imports normally. Wrapping the fetch/parse (and possibly per-item import) in `begin/rescue` is a concrete robustness fix for this new behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicRetriever#fetch_http` perform server-side fetches of attacker-influenced URLs (open-uri, default redirect-following).**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces server-side fetching of a URL derived from request input. `EmbedController#best` takes `params.require(:embed_url)` and enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, which calls `TopicRetriever.new(args[:embed_url]).retrieve`. `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` then calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (open-uri). Although `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, the fetched URL is still attacker-influenced within that host and open-uri will follow redirects by default without re-validating the destination host, enabling SSRF-style pivots via redirects (and potentially arbitrary ports on the allowed host). Also, the referer-based check in `ensure_embeddable` relies on a header that can be spoofed by non-browser clients, so an attacker can trigger these fetches if they know the configured embeddable host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:29` (`open(url).read`) — the host must match `embeddable_host`, but path/query is attacker-controlled, and `open-uri` follows redirects by default; a malicious or compromised target page could redirect the server to internal/other resources (SSRF surface). Given this era's `open-uri`, this is worth hardening rather than assuming it's safe.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` on a URL that can originate from user-controlled input (`embed_url` param -> `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: ...)` -> `TopicRetriever` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). While `TopicRetriever` checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, that validation only applies to the initially supplied URL. `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects by default, and the code does not constrain redirects or re-validate the final destination host/IP, so a URL on the allowed host could redirect the server to other/internal resources (SSRF via redirect). Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is also called directly from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` without any host restriction at all, widening the SSRF surface if that task is run on untrusted input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **How to fix**: pin `open-uri` behavior (disable redirects or validate the redirect target's host as well), and/or use a proper HTTP client with an explicit allowlist and timeout.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` and it is exercised in the spec via `TopicEmbed.import` on creation (the spec asserts rewritten `` and `` values). While it’s true the update-path spec doesn’t include link/img cases and there are no tests for edge cases like non-default ports, that is a test-coverage suggestion rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Why it matters**: these are precisely the code paths carrying untrusted external content (see Critical #1) — they need direct tests, including a security-oriented test asserting dangerous tags/attributes are stripped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new code paths that ingest and render external content: `Jobs::PollFeed` unescapes and imports `i.content` from an RSS/ATOM feed, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches arbitrary remote HTML via `open(url).read`. That content is persisted into `Post#raw` with `cook_method: :raw_html`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` uses Rails' dependency-tracking require on a third-party gem; should just be `require 'nokogiri'`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` in `TopicEmbed`. While `require_dependency` is primarily meant for Rails autoload/reload tracking, it still delegates to `require` and will successfully load a gem like `nokogiri` as long as it’s in the Gemfile (which it is via `ruby-readability`/existing deps). This is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the change—at most it’s an unnecessary/idiomatic preference (style) to use `require` for third-party gems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused dead code (nothing in the file references `Email::Sender`).

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb the constant Email::Sender is never referenced; the job only looks up a User and calls TopicRetriever. However, an extra require_dependency that isn’t referenced is at most a minor cleanup/performance nit, and it’s not a verifiable correctness/bug/security defect introduced by the diff (it could also exist for side effects/autoloading patterns outside this file).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15` — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check rather than an exact-origin comparison; prefer `e.origin !== discourseUrl` (or compare parsed origins) for a precise, non-surprising check even though `discourseUrl` isn't attacker-controlled here.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that using `indexOf` for origin validation is a substring check and recommends exact-origin (or parsed-origin) comparison, which is the same weakness described in the golden comment (bypass via a malicious domain containing the trusted domain as a substring).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `config/locales/server.en.yml` — `embed.permalink` key is added but never referenced anywhere in the views/models.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink` to `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and there is no reference to `t('embed.permalink')` / `I18n.t('embed.permalink')` in the new embed views (`best.html.erb`, `loading.html.erb`, `embed.html.erb`) or other added Ruby code. However, an unused i18n key is not a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect; it’s at most dead/extra locale data and could be intended for future UI work. adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb` — `ensure_embeddable` only supports a single `embeddable_host`; no path to allow multiple embedding domains without redeploying config. Consider a comma-separated list if that's a plausible near-term need.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces a single `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and enforces it via `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` in `ensure_embeddable`. This is a design choice/feature limitation, not a verifiable bug or defect introduced by the change. Also, the finding’s claim about needing a redeploy is not grounded in the diff: `embeddable_host` is a site setting (in `config/site_settings.yml`) and is typically configurable at runtime via admin settings, not code redeploy. There is no evidence in the diff that multiple domains are required or that the single-host behavior breaks correctness/security relative to stated requirements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best` — if `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns a stale `topic_id` for a topic that's since been deleted/made private, `TopicView.new` will raise unrescued (500 instead of a graceful "not found"/loading state).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the presence of a `topic_id` from `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is treated as sufficient to build `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` with no validation that the referenced topic still exists or is accessible. The new `topic_embeds` table has no foreign key constraints, so it is possible for `topic_embeds.topic_id`/`post_id` to become stale (e.g., topic deleted) while the row remains. In that case `TopicView.new` will typically need to load the topic/post and can raise (e.g., record not found / access error), and this controller does not rescue and fall back to the loading/enqueue path. The exact HTTP status (500 vs framework-mapped 404/403) depends on how exceptions are handled elsewhere, but the diff does introduce an unhandled-exception path when `topic_id` is stale.
